chapters.caption: Deepa Iyer has invested. Operations open her portal account from her page.
Her Account panel says she has no account yet.
Invite to the portal makes the account and emails her a link to set her own password. Nobody at Moneybee sees it.
The link works once, for seven days. Her timeline says it went, and until when.
This is the email she receives.
Client accounts lists every account with its status and last sign-in. Hers reads Invited until she signs in.
Deals shows every prospective investment by stage. This is the PMS board.
The line under the title adds up the open deals and counts the ones with nothing planned.
Ananya Bose: Rs. 2 crore, three days at Contacted, and No next step in amber.
To move a deal, hover its card and press Move. You can also click the card and press M.
Pick the stage it has reached. Meeting asks one thing first.
When and where. The time starts on the next working day at 11:00.
Leave Then write the Meeting confirmation ticked, and press Move to Meeting.
Her page opens with the Meeting confirmation written, the time and place filled in.
The meeting is in her tasks now, so the deal has a next step.
Back on the board, her card shows the meeting where No next step was.
When the money lands, move her to Invested. It asks the amount and the date.
Operations see one more box here: Invite to the portal. Press Move to Invested.
For a PMS client the Welcome letter opens next, with the account date filled in.
Every move is a line on her timeline, with who made it.
Enquiries lists every message from the Contact page, most urgent first, each with the time its reply is due.
Opening one shows what they sent, and on the right, when the reply is due and what the playbook asks.
Take it, so the desk knows it is yours. The playbook's steps become your tasks.
Start from a template. The PMS introduction fills in the words and brings the latest fact sheet with it.
Here email is not connected yet, so the reply is saved on the timeline. Once it is, the button says Send reply.
When they are serious, turn the enquiry into a deal with the amount they mentioned.
Their page holds everything about them: the reply, the deal and the tasks.
Log the call you made. No answer suggests calling again the next working day at 10:00.
The call-back is now one of your tasks, and the call is on the timeline.
Sanjay Agarwal wrote in about Flyingbee, and said he invests as an HUF.
The Person panel offers to record the HUF. Give its name as on its PAN.
Now it says he invests through the Agarwal Family HUF. Others in the family can be linked to the same one by its name.
A deal opened from here carries the HUF.
On the Flyingbee board, his card shows the HUF under his name.
Priya Menon is due the fee illustration today. Write opens her page on the letter.
Write your words. Dear Priya Menon and your signature are added for you.
Attach adds any file Moneybee keeps, or a new one from your computer.
Pick the file. It goes with this one email only.
Save it. Sending ticks the task, since this was the letter it asked for.
Files shows every file kept. The panel says where each is used and every email it went in.
Today is where each day starts: what is waiting on Moneybee, what is late, and your own tasks.
Each count opens its list. Anything above zero needs someone.
Below them, your own tasks for today, the overdue ones first.
Everything else is in the menu. Desk holds the daily work: enquiries, tasks, people and deals.
Tasks lists everything you owe someone, grouped by when it is due.
Press T on any screen to add a task without leaving what you are doing.
Every screen opens with a line on what it is for. How to use this brings you to its entry in the Guide.
The Guide explains every screen, with pictures and videos like this one.
Kunal Shah met the team, then chose another manager. His card shows the meeting still planned.
Move the deal to Lost. It asks why.
Pick the reason, and add a line if it will help whoever talks to him next.
Moving to Lost closes the deal's open tasks, so nobody calls him by mistake.
Lost deals stay at the end of the board for 90 days. Click it to open.
Each lost card keeps its reason.
On his page, the move and each closed task are on the timeline.
People lists everyone who has written in or invests. A name opens their page.
Their page has everything about them. The box at the top is for writing to them or logging what happened.
Email sends any letter that can go to them: a reply on their enquiry, a client letter, or your own words.
Note leaves a line for whoever opens her page next.
The timeline shows everything that has happened, newest first. The filters narrow it.
On the right, one panel per decision: her tasks, enquiries, deal and account.
Mine shows what you owe, overdue first, then today, tomorrow and later.
Each task is done from its row. A call shows the number to ring.
An email has Write. It opens her page on the letter, and sending it ticks the task.
Tick a task when it is done.
Then say what happened, so the next person knows. Or Undo, or add the next task.
Team shows everyone's open tasks, with who owns each.
Asked of others shows the tasks you gave someone else, and Done the last two weeks.
